Jointly estimate a group-level choice-model shape and refine the group embedding

estimate_group_alpha.Rd

run_group_embedding_from_list always fits the group embedding under the crowd-kernel choice model (\(\alpha = 1\) on the Student-t continuum used throughout this package's recovery/validation work: \(\alpha = 1\) is exactly crowd-kernel \(\mu = 1\), \(\alpha \to \infty\) is the exact Gaussian limit). This function takes that fit as a starting point and alternates, via coordinate ascent, between (1) re-estimating \(\alpha\) by profiled maximum likelihood with the embedding held fixed, and (2) refitting the embedding under the current \(\alpha\), warm-started from the previous iteration – the group-level analogue of the per-participant joint estimation done by condor_joint_manifold_workflow.py's update step (vignette("condor_workflows_vignette"), Workflow 4), but simpler: there is only one \(\alpha\) and one embedding to estimate, so no cross-participant pooling or empirical-Bayes shrinkage is needed.

Usage

estimate_group_alpha(
  triplet_list,
  warm_start,
  max_epochs = 50000L,
  tolerance = 1e-04,
  tol_window = 10000L,
  seed = 222L,
  device = NULL,
  norm_penalty = 0,
  max_outer = 15L,
  tol_log_alpha = 0.05,
  alpha_grid = 10^seq(log10(2e-04), log10(2e+06), length.out = 140),
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

triplet_list

A named list of data frames, one per participant, as returned by get.combined – the same object passed to run_group_embedding_from_list to produce warm_start. Must contain genuine sampleAlg == "validation" trials (see Details).

warm_start

Numeric matrix giving the starting embedding: one row per item (row names = item names) and d columns, typically the embedding returned by a prior call to run_group_embedding_from_list on the same triplet_list. Required – this function refines an already-fit embedding rather than fitting one from scratch. d is taken from ncol(warm_start).

max_epochs, tolerance, tol_window, device, norm_penalty

Same meaning as the matching arguments of run_group_embedding_from_list, applied to every embedding-refit step.

seed

Integer random seed, used for the train/test shuffling fallback (when triplet_list has no usable sampleSet split) and as the embedding fit's random_state at every outer iteration.

max_outer

Maximum number of coordinate-ascent iterations. Default 15.

tol_log_alpha

Convergence threshold on the log scale: stop once the re-estimated \(\alpha\) changes by less than this between iterations. Default 0.05.

alpha_grid

Candidate \(\alpha\) values for the profiled maximum-likelihood step at each iteration.

verbose

Logical; print one line of progress per outer iteration. Default TRUE.

Value

A named list with five elements:

embedding

Numeric matrix, the final refit embedding (item names as row names, dim_0/dim_1/... columns).

alpha

Final estimated \(\alpha\).

log_alpha

log(alpha).

ci

95\ \(\alpha\) at the final iteration.

history

Data frame with one row per outer iteration: iter, alpha, ll_val (validation log-likelihood at the re-estimated \(\alpha\)), acc_val (validation accuracy), epoch (embedding-refit stopping epoch), and delta_log_alpha.

Details

\(\alpha\) is re-estimated at each iteration using only sampleAlg == "validation" trials – genuinely held out, never used to fit the embedding at any iteration. This is deliberate: profiling \(\alpha\) on the same trials the embedding was just optimized against would let the \(\alpha\) estimate chase training noise the embedding has already been shaped to fit, rather than measuring real choice-model shape. triplet_list must therefore contain real validation trials (see set_validation_behavior/assign_sample_sets to designate some, or find_frequent_triplets/ assign_validation_from_frequency to retrofit a validation set onto legacy data that predates that convention).

Iteration stops once the re-estimated \(\alpha\) changes by less than tol_log_alpha (on the log scale) from the previous iteration, or after max_outer iterations, whichever comes first.

What this does and does not estimate

Unlike the per-participant joint workflow, there is no population of noisy per-person \(\alpha\) estimates to shrink toward each other here – a single \(\alpha\) is estimated from the whole pooled dataset directly, with no regularization pulling it back if it is poorly identified. Check ci (the final iteration's 95\ confidence interval) before trusting the point estimate, especially on a small dataset or at large \(\alpha\) (the Student-t kernel converges to Gaussian as \(\alpha\) grows, so the profile likelihood flattens and \(\alpha\) becomes harder to pin down precisely, even though validation accuracy itself is structurally insensitive to \(\alpha\) for this choice-model family and so cannot reveal this on its own).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
grp <- run_group_embedding_from_list(icon_triplets, d = 3L)
joint <- estimate_group_alpha(icon_triplets, warm_start = grp$embedding)
joint$alpha
joint$history
} # }
